# Essentials — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other Essentials: typically around 750, most listings 80–15,000 (43 listings)
- Household: typically around 950, most listings 570–15,000 (10 listings)
- Healthcare: typically around 1,500, most listings 600–2,000 (8 listings — thin data)
- Grocery: typically around 500, most listings 200–2,300 (7 listings — thin data)

This is a low-ticket category, so a low price is rarely a scam signal here; be more alert to
absurdly high prices on everyday consumables (e.g. five figures for a small hygiene or grocery
item), which suggest a mispost or price typo. Healthcare and Grocery have under 10 listings
each — treat those ranges as rough and lean on general judgment.

## What good listings look like
- "Bona Papa Extra Soft Baby wipes Pack of 10 (Value Deal)" — NPR 700
- "Dot & Key Ceramides & Hyaluronic Barrier Repair Moisturizer With Probiotics & Rice Water (100 g)" — NPR 749
- "Plates at just 960 for 6" — NPR 960
- "bed bug spray" — NPR 850
- "whole kitchen set up on sale" — NPR 14,000

A good Essentials listing names the brand, pack size or quantity, and (for consumables)
that the item is new/sealed; prices sit in the everyday-retail range above.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Healthcare listings claiming to treat, cure, or slim (e.g. "weight loss capsule",
  miracle supplements) or reselling pharmacy-only medicines person-to-person → hold;
  ordinary retail cosmetics/hygiene products (moisturizer, wipes) are fine.
- Wrong-category posts are common here — live samples include guitars, crochet flower
  bouquets, and bracelets filed under Essentials. Obvious non-essentials → hold so an
  editor can recategorize.
- Rejection history is nearly empty (one case: photos that didn't look legitimate), so
  beyond the above, do not add extra strictness — default to normal judgment.
